title: A Terminal for the Horizon Again
premise: August Coldharbour, a xenolinguist whose dreams have turned alien, is hauling cargo through contested orbits when gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds—a signal he alone recognizes as the death-cry of a station that officially never existed. To prove the Meridian Massacre happened, he must decode the flicker's embedded testimony before the ruling Concordat finishes rewriting every record and memory in the system. Pursued by an archivist who erases history and haunted by the inheritance of his mother's stolen research, August learns the massacre's true target was a language that could store memory outside human minds. In the end, he broadcasts the testimony in that alien tongue—unreadable to the Concordat, but permanent in every dreamer who hears it—and surrenders his own records, becoming the last human archive of a crime the universe itself now remembers.
about_author: Edmund Ishikawa is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing signals no one claimed to have sent. He writes from a decommissioned lighthouse, where he insists the fog still carries old frequencies.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: August's POV. While hauling ore past the contested Verge, gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, crews scream, then everything resumes as if nothing happened. August alone dreams that night in a language he cannot speak awake. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: The Station That Was Never Built
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following the flicker's resonance, he finds Meridian Station—officially unbuilt—drifting dark and scoured, its corridors scrubbed of names but not of sound. He records a residual acoustic ghost in the walls. Emotional beat: vertigo of confronting erased history, first proof he isn't crazy.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifests and Ghost Tongues
chapters.summary: August's POV, intercut with his dead mother's research logs. He realizes the flicker was a compressed testimony in a xenolinguistic structure his mother theorized decades ago: memory encoded outside human minds. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Clean Pages
chapters.summary: Sable Venn's POV, the Concordat's chief record-keeper. She detects an unregistered signal from Meridian and dispatches erasure teams, revealing the Concordat's doctrine: history is a maintenance problem. Emotional beat: chilling competence, the antagonist's sincere belief she is protecting civilization.

chapters.title: Allies in Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: August's POV. He recruits his old crew—engineer Dessa, who lost family at Meridian, and smuggler-priest Okafor, who keeps forbidden oral records. They decode the first fragment: the station's inhabitants didn't die in an accident; they were silenced for what they learned to say. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: What the Concordat Burned
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Raiding a Concordat memory-vault, the crew finds physical evidence—pre-rewrite manifests—plus a horrifying discovery: the Concordat doesn't just erase records, it edits implanted memory-chips in citizens. Emotional beat: outrage and despair; the past itself is occupied territory.

chapters.title: The Language That Dreams Back
chapters.summary: August's POV. Decoding deepens; the xenolanguage begins answering him, reconstructing the massacre's final hours in his dreams until he can no longer tell which memories are his. Emotional beat: dissolution of self, the price of testimony—memory as both inheritance and infection.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Verge
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. Cornered by Venn's erasure fleet, the crew learns someone sold their route—and it's Dessa, coerced with the promise of her family's restored records. Venn offers August the same bargain: his mother's name cleansed, his freedom, in exchange for the testimony. Emotional beat: temptation, betrayal as love twisted by power.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. Rather than surrender the testimony, August hijacks the system-wide gravity lattice itself—the same infrastructure that carried the flicker—to broadcast the massacre in the xenolanguage, making it unerasable because it lives in every dreaming mind. Venn's fleets can kill him but not the signal. Emotional beat: sacrifice, defiance, power reclaimed as witness.

chapters.title: A Terminal for the Horizon Again
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue. Imprisoned and officially forgotten, August finds the Concordat cannot erase what now surfaces in millions of dreams; inquiries begin, and Dessa, freed, carries his mother's restored research onward. August dreams in human languages again, for the first time in years. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—memory outlives its keepers.
